items.summary: Every save-loading message in parse.ts now says what is likely wrong and what to do, with no JSON, gzip, schema or version numbers. Not a save: 'This file is not a HumanBench save. Choose the file you downloaded ... or paste a save code.' for a chosen file, and 'This is not a HumanBench save or save code. Choose your downloaded save file, or paste the save code you copied.' for pasted text (the loader now knows which it was). Invalid JSON: 'looks cut off or damaged'. Empty, too large (file, pasted text, unpacked save), newer version, cannot-open, damaged and unreadable paste each have their own next step. The developer reason (migrate.ts message) moved to ParseFailure.details; error codes are unchanged. Every message that is a 'not a save' keeps the substring 'not a HumanBench save'.

extra_fixes.summary: Found by session-save.spec.ts with the session package's new run guard: SessionApp.svelte (session-owned, UX-011) calls installUnloadGuard() from reveal/guard.ts while the run is in progress. guard.ts used ONE shared listener, so when the results screen mounted its own guard (Reveal.svelte) the second addEventListener was ignored as a duplicate, and when SessionApp lifted its guard it removed the only listener: the results were unguarded ('the tab asks before closing while the file is not saved' failed on all three projects). installUnloadGuard now installs its own listener per call, so overlapping guards are independent.
tests_added: guard.test.ts and guard.dom.test.ts: two overlapping guards, lifting the first leaves the second on (fake target and the real window)
